codeReview.summary: The SimBroker has been upgraded from a simple Vec recorder to a functional mock MQTT broker with 6 new features (QoS 1 tracking, subscription matching, loss rate, disconnect/reconnect, dropped count), all off by default. Implementation is clean, well-documented with module-level doc comments, and includes 10 new tests covering all features plus edge cases and interactions. The TDD process was followed correctly (RED→GREEN visible in transcript). All 63 launa-sim tests pass, and full workspace passes (371 tests).

issues.description: Packet ID wrapping: when next_packet_id reaches u16::MAX (65535), subsequent calls reuse IDs starting from 1. If old entries with matching IDs are still unacked in the HashMap, they'll be silently overwritten. This is acceptable for a test mock but could cause confusing test failures if a test publishes >65535 QoS 1 messages without acking. No action needed — just worth noting as a known limitation.

publish_qos1 returns 0 to indicate a dropped publish (due to disconnect/loss). In real MQTT, packet ID 0 is invalid, so this is a reasonable sentinel. However, the API has no documentation or method to distinguish 'dropped due to disconnect' from 'dropped due to loss rate'. The test test_simbroker_disconnect_drops_qos1 only checks disconnect. If a test needed to distinguish these cases, it couldn't. Acceptable for current requirements.

sharedStateObservations.observation: architecture.md states 'All workspace crates are `#![no_std]` with `extern crate alloc`' but launa-sim has never been no_std — it uses `std` features from launa-hal and launa-mqtt, and sim_broker.rs imports `std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet}`. This invariant description is inaccurate for launa-sim. The mission AGENTS.md also states 'All workspace crates must remain `#![no_std]`' but launa-sim is a desktop-only simulation crate.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: architecture.md 'Invariants' section, launa-sim/Cargo.toml has `launa-hal = { path = "../launa-hal", features = ["std"] }`, sim_broker.rs line 20 uses `std::collections`

summary: PASS. The SimBroker upgrade is well-implemented, follows TDD correctly, covers all 6 required features with 10 tests (exceeds the 5+ requirement), maintains full backward compatibility (all features off by default), and passes all 371 workspace tests with no regressions.
